name: datasets/exchange-rates
what_it_holds: Frictionless-Data/Open Knowledge Foundation packaged FX dataset sourced from FRED (fred.stlouisfed.org). Daily, monthly and yearly CSVs with Date, Country, Value fields (USD/currency or currency/USD by country convention). Datapackage.json schema included; automated maintenance workflow.
why_useful: Ready-to-use multi-country FX time series in tidy CSV form, no API key needed -- can substitute/cross-check our current FRED FX pull (~40 series) with a pre-packaged, versioned alternative and is trivially reproducible.
last_activity: 55 commits, automated update workflow present (exact date not shown)
time_coverage: Historical through FRED's series length (varies by currency, several decades for majors)
duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps with our existing FRED FX schedules holding; flagged because it is a pre-cleaned, versioned CSV mirror rather than a raw API pull
themes: FX and purchasing power: exchange-rate history (ECB, BIS, FRED), broad-dollar indices, PPP/Big Mac, tourist affordability indices, company FX-exposure tooling
wildcard: an FX and macro strategist who models translation effects an
why_all: Ready-to-use multi-country FX time series in tidy CSV form, no API key needed -- can substitute/cross-check our current FRED FX pull (~40 series) with a pre-packaged, versioned alternative and is trivially reproducible.
Wider currency coverage than our current FX schedule for translation-effect modeling of ABNB's regional revenue mix, especially smaller LatAm/APAC currencies.

name: fawazahmed0/exchange-api (successor to currency-api)
what_it_holds: Git-based, daily-updated JSON currency exchange rate files (200+ currencies, plus crypto/metals) served via jsDelivr/Cloudflare CDN, but the underlying data is committed to the git history day by day -- so cloning history gives a de facto daily point-in-time FX panel back to when the project started (repo shows queries working from at least 2024-03-06 forward; older history may exist in git log). Prettified and minified JSON per date.
why_useful: Because each day's rates are a separate git-tracked JSON snapshot, this is one of the few free FX sources that is inherently point-in-time/vintage-correct (rule #2) rather than a rewritten current-value table -- useful for reconstructing what a spot rate looked like on any specific historical date without paying for a vendor terminal.
last_activity: 111 commits, active GitHub Actions daily publish workflow
time_coverage: Daily, from project start (~2023) to present
size_hint: many small JSON files, cumulative history could be sizeable via git log
duplicate_of_holding: New angle vs our existing FX schedules: vintage-correctness via git history
themes: FX and purchasing power: exchange-rate history (ECB, BIS, FRED), broad-dollar indices, PPP/Big Mac, tourist affordability indices, company FX-exposure tooling

name: expersso/BIS
what_it_holds: R package with get_datasets() and get_bis() functions that download and parse BIS (Bank for International Settlements) CSV datasets into a unified format: policy rates, exchange rates, nominal and real effective exchange rate (EER) indices, credit statistics, property prices, at daily/monthly/quarterly/annual frequencies.
why_useful: Gives a one-command pull of BIS broad effective exchange rate indices (a standard 'broad-dollar-index' analogue for other currencies, e.g. EUR EER, JPY EER) that we do not currently hold -- useful for constructing a multi-currency trade-weighted FX basket beyond just USD, relevant to ABNB's EMEA/APAC/LatAm revenue mix.
license: not explicitly shown on page (unofficial/community R package, unaffiliated with BIS)
last_activity: 6 commits (low activity, but BIS's own data endpoints are stable)
time_coverage: BIS EER series generally 1994-present per BIS's own archive
size_hint: small R package, data pulled live from BIS servers (not committed)
themes: FX and purchasing power: exchange-rate history (ECB, BIS, FRED), broad-dollar indices, PPP/Big Mac, tourist affordability indices, company FX-exposure tooling

name: sie_banxico
what_it_holds: Small Python wrapper (MIT, 4 stars) for Banco de Mexico's Sistema de Informacion Economica (SIE) API. Documents example series like SF311408/SF311418 (monetary aggregates M1/M2); supports metadata lookup, latest value, historical range queries, percent-change calc, pandas output. Code only, no committed data.
why_useful: One-command pull for Mexican peso FX and macro series (consumer strength / FX gap #7 and #6) at whatever frequency Banxico publishes; complements Mexico City nights forecast with a real-time peso/rate input.
time_coverage: as far back as each SIE series goes (many decades for FX/CPI)
themes: Regional macro for LatAm and APAC: Mexico INEGI/Banxico, Brazil IBGE/BCB, Argentina INDEC, Colombia DANE, Chile, Japan e-Stat, Korea KOSIS, Australia ABS, India MOSPI clients
why_all: One-command pull for Mexican peso FX and macro series (consumer strength / FX gap #7 and #6) at whatever frequency Banxico publishes; complements Mexico City nights forecast with a real-time peso/rate input.

Gap #7 (Mexico regional macro) -- Mexico City is in our Inside Airbnb panel; Banxico SIE carries FX, monetary and (via other series codes) tourism/travel-balance-of-payments indicators (travel receipts) that could feed a Mexico-specific ADR/FX or demand proxy.

name: griddedGDPpc
what_it_holds: Academic replication package (R + Matlab + Python scripts, no data files committed in repo root) for 'Downscaled gridded global dataset for GDP per capita at purchasing power parity (PPP) over 1990-2024, constant 2021 USD'. Global coverage, ADM0/ADM1/ADM2 admin levels plus gridded rasters (5 arcmin/30 arcmin/30 arcsec GeoTIFF) and GeoPackage+CSV tables, combining World Bank/IMF/CIA national data with OECD/Eurostat subnational detail. Actual output data lives on Zenodo (linked from paper: Kummu et al. 2025, Scientific Data 12:567), not in this GitHub repo. MIT-licensed code.
why_useful: Gives a country-by-country and subnational PPP-adjusted GDP per capita time series, which is a structural proxy for cross-border travel affordability and currency-adjusted consumer spending power feeding ABNB's international ADR/nights mix (relevant to gap themes on FX mix and regional consumer strength, e.g. overlapping with the existing FX-mix / consumer-strength-regional-split workstreams).
size_hint: code repo only (~20 scripts); actual data hosted on Zenodo, size unknown from this fetch
license: MIT (code); data license unspecified in README, check Zenodo
themes: Currency and travel affordability crowdsourced data: Numbeo, Expatistan, hotel price indices (Hotels.com HPI archives), Trivago Hotel Price Index, Kayak price trackers
why_all: Gives a country-by-country and subnational PPP-adjusted GDP per capita time series, which is a structural proxy for cross-border travel affordability and currency-adjusted consumer spending power feeding ABNB's international ADR/nights mix (relevant to gap themes on FX mix and regional consumer strength, e.g. overlapping with the existing FX-mix / consumer-strength-regional-split workstreams).
